__comment: The Park Bulletin (/now). One file per NPS Yosemite Guide edition. When the park publishes a new Guide (roughly every five weeks), rewrite this file from it, then (1) bump the shared ?v= on BULLETIN_URL (page-now.jsx), HOME_BULLETIN_URL (page-home.jsx) and TIOGA_BULLETIN_URL (page-tioga-opening.jsx), (2) run `npm --prefix scripts run compile`, `npm --prefix scripts run seo` and `npm --prefix scripts run assets:stamp`, (3) commit. `node scripts/check-bulletin.mjs` (part of `npm --prefix scripts run check`) validates every field named here. Facts come from the printed Guide plus park sources; a row the Guide does not carry is a row this file does not carry. Every date is ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) and the page reads it against today's date in Yosemite, so nothing here is written relative to a day ('tomorrow', 'this week'): the page works that out, which is what lets one file stay correct for five weeks. FIELDS. edition: label, start, end, updated (drives the /now sitemap lastmod and the deploy-parity stamp), lede (original house copy, no em-dashes), source, sourceUrl, and an optional notice, one sentence shown above everything (the stale-edition note goes here). headlines: two to four tiles carrying the edition's most important facts, { label, icon, status, tone, text }; tone is open | warn | closed; icon is a BULLETIN_ICONS name from page-now.jsx, optional, and restates what the text already says, never a new fact (an unknown name renders the neutral mark). changes: the dated ledger the page splits at today into 'Coming up' and 'Already closed', { date, when, kind, what, detail }. kind is closes | ends | hours | opens | event. date is the date the Guide gives: on and before it the row is coming up, after it the row has happened (a past closes or ends row lists under 'Already closed', a past hours row under 'Hours changed', and a past opens or event row drops off, because the schedule carries it). when is an optional display label that replaces the date ('Early October', with date set to the day it sorts by); a row with no date is season-long and when names its group ('This season', 'Out of order'). areas: { name, chip, tone, note }, read by /now, by /tioga-opening (the Tioga row) and by the crawler prose. programAreas: the schedule's tabs, { key, name, short, notes }, notes being [{ h, t }] for the area's standing extras that are not a timed row. programs: every timed program and dated event in the Guide, { area, time, title, detail, detailByDay, where, days, from, until, dates, except, fee, access, allAges, tag }. area is a programAreas key, or 'parkwide' for a park-wide event, which shows above every area's list and may omit time. time is the Guide's start time ('9:00 am', 'Noon'). days is 'daily' or a list of su mo tu we th fr sa. from and until bound a run, inclusive. dates lists the exact days of a one-off or scattered event and replaces days; except removes single dates. detailByDay maps a day code to that day's detail. fee marks a paid, ticketed or registered-and-paid row. access and allAges are the printed Guide's own per-program symbols (wheelchair accessible, recommended for families), read off the Programs page row by row and true-only, because an unmarked program is one the Guide did not mark rather than one it ruled out. The same two marks ride the PWA's program feed as accessible / familyFriendly (workers/src/data/manual-programs.ts); re-read both from the new Programs page every edition. tag is an optional short label ('Exhibit', 'Last of the season'); one-day rows are labelled by the page. programsNote: the schedule's footnote. trails: { name, chip, tone, distance, start, note }; open rows list under 'Open as usual', warn and closed rows under 'Check before you go'. hours: groups of { name, hours, note, closes, then }; closes is the last open day, after which the row reads Closed, and then is { from, hours }, the hours from that date on. transit: { name, note, until }, until being the last day a seasonal service runs. essentials: { title, text }. numbers: { label, value }.

edition.label: August 19 – September 22, 2026
edition.lede: The edition where summer ends. Every road is still open and the high country is at its best, but the waterfalls are down to their bones and the park starts shutting for the season in the first two weeks of September: the High Sierra Camps, the pools, the Tuolumne store and grill, the hikers bus. Go high while you can.
edition.source: Condensed from the National Park Service Yosemite Guide for August 19 – September 22, 2026, with the journal's own notes.

headlines.label: Roads
headlines.text: Tioga and Glacier Point included. Weekday delays of about 15 minutes at El Capitan Bridge, 7 am to 7 pm through December, and on Big Oak Flat Road between Foresta and Crane Flat. On Tioga Road, 10 minutes through Tuolumne Meadows and 15 minutes from Olmsted Point to Tioga Pass, 8 am to 3:30 pm Monday to Thursday.

headlines.label: Dome Fire
headlines.text: Northeast of Wawona, smoke around the park and periods of unhealthy air at some hours. The Chilnualna Falls trail is closed, and the trails above it toward Buena Vista and Crescent Lakes with it.

headlines.label: Valley parking
headlines.text: Arrive before 8 am or after 4 pm, park once, and ride the free shuttles. Text ynptraffic to 333111 for traffic alerts.

headlines.label: Mist Trail
headlines.text: 7 am to 3:30 pm for repairs, through October. Open Friday to Sunday, holidays, and outside those hours. The John Muir Trail detour is signed.

areas.name: Yosemite Valley
areas.note: Busy by mid-morning, worse on weekends, and quieter after Labor Day. Parking in three hubs: Curry Village, Yosemite Village, Yosemite Falls. Once parked, stay parked and ride the free shuttles.

areas.name: Tioga Road & Tuolumne Meadows
areas.note: The 39-mile high-country drive, 6,200 to nearly 10,000 feet. Little to no cell service; fuel and plan before you go. The lodge closed Sep 13 and its dining room and grill Sep 14 by the concessioner's dates; the store runs through Sep 20 per the Guide, and the area shuttle stopped Sep 13. Construction delays on the drive: 10 minutes through the meadows, 15 minutes from Olmsted Point to Tioga Pass, 8 am to 3:30 pm Monday to Thursday. The trail between the wilderness center and Lembert Dome is closed for construction, with an alternate signed.

areas.name: Glacier Point Road
areas.note: One hour from the Valley. No trailers or vehicles over 30 feet past the Sentinel Dome trailhead. The gift shop runs 9 am to 7 pm.

areas.name: Wawona & Mariposa Grove
areas.note: An hour south of the Valley. Free grove shuttle every 15 minutes, 8 am to 7 pm, last bus down at 8 pm. The Dome Fire is burning northeast of Wawona: the Chilnualna Falls trail and the trails above it are closed, and the smoke comes and goes. The hotel is closed for renovation and the stable finished Sep 6.

areas.name: Crane Flat
areas.note: Thirty minutes up Big Oak Flat Road, and the quiet way to see sequoias: Tuolumne Grove 2 miles round trip, Merced Grove 3. Information station and wilderness permits 8 am to 5 pm.

areas.name: Hetch Hetchy
areas.note: An hour and a half from the Valley. No services, very little shade, and hot into September. No vehicles or trailers over 25 feet long or 8 feet wide on the entrance road, and no pets on the dam or the trails.

areas.name: Gas
areas.note: El Portal 15 miles downhill on 140, Crane Flat 16.5 miles uphill on Big Oak Flat Road, Wawona 28 miles up Wawona Road. All pump 24 hours with a card.

programsNote: Everything unmarked is free and drop-in. The accessible and all-ages marks are the Yosemite Guide's own symbols: accessible means the program is held in a wheelchair-accessible facility or uses wheelchair-accessible paths, and the park asks you to raise any other accommodation with the program host. An unmarked program is one the Guide did not mark, not one it ruled out.

trails.name: Mist Trail to Vernal & Nevada Falls
trails.distance: Footbridge 1.6 mi, 380 ft · top of Vernal 2.4 mi, 1,000 ft · top of Nevada 5 mi, 2,000 ft
trails.note: Closed M – Th, 7 am – 3:30 pm for repairs through the end of October; open F – Su, holidays, and outside those hours when conditions allow. Use the signed John Muir Trail detour during the closure. Looping back on the John Muir Trail by Clark Point makes Vernal 3.7 miles and Nevada 5.8.

trails.name: Chilnualna Falls
trails.note: Closed for the Dome Fire, along with the trails from the top toward Buena Vista and Crescent Lakes. No reopening date announced. Check the park's conditions page before driving down.

trails.name: Half Dome
trails.note: The cables are up, which means a permit every day of the week, and they typically come down in the first half of October. Daily lottery two days ahead on Recreation.gov, applications midnight to 4 pm. Be honest about the day.

trails.name: Lower Yosemite Fall
trails.note: East side wheelchair-accessible. The fall is done for the season and returns with the first autumn storms. Go for the amphitheater and the scale of the wall.

trails.name: Mirror Lake
trails.distance: 2 mi, 100 ft on the paved road · 4.5 mi around the basin
trails.note: The lakebed is a meadow this time of year. Leashed pets on the paved road only; a valid disability placard may drive it.

trails.name: Bridalveil Fall
trails.note: Paved to a wheelchair-accessible viewing area, steeper to the base. Thin but still showing in the afternoon wind. Stay behind the barriers: the rocks at the base are slick.

trails.name: Cook's Meadow
trails.note: Pavement and boardwalk. Half Dome and Yosemite Falls views; best light early and late, and the birds are out at both ends of the day.

trails.name: Yosemite Falls Trail
trails.distance: Columbia Rock 2 mi · the top 7.2 mi, 2,700 ft
trails.note: Columbia Rock earns the view. The full climb is six to eight hours and dozens of switchbacks: start at dawn.

trails.name: Four Mile Trail
trails.note: To Glacier Point, six to eight hours. One-way option: ride the tour bus up, walk down. Drop-offs only at the point, no pickup.

trails.name: Valley Loop Trail
trails.note: Mostly flat but uneven, and the quietest miles on the floor. The El Capitan Bridge section is closed on weekdays through December for bridge work, so on a weekday walk the north and south sides as two out-and-backs, or come on a weekend for the full loop. No pets or bikes.

trails.name: Sentinel Dome & Taft Point
trails.distance: Taft Point 2.4 mi · Sentinel Dome 1.8 mi
trails.note: One trailhead, two rim walks: Taft Point to the west, Sentinel Dome to the northeast.

trails.name: Tuolumne & Merced Groves
trails.distance: Tuolumne 2 mi, 500 ft · Merced 3 mi, 520 ft
trails.note: The uncrowded sequoias. You walk down first, so save the legs for the return.

trailsNote: Overnights require a wilderness permit year-round, and a bear canister; rent one at permit pickup. Carry a quart of water per person for every two hours, three for the falls corridor, plus salty snacks, a headlamp, a map, and a layer. Turn around when half the water is gone. No pets or bikes on any hiking trail. Big-wall climbers self-register for overnight permits at the kiosk near shuttle stop 9.

transit.name: Valley shuttles
transit.note: Free, daily 7 am – 10 pm, year-round. Valleywide green line hits every stop, every 22 – 32 minutes, an hour and a half round trip; the purple East Valley line runs every 18 – 22 minutes, 50 minutes round trip. No pets.

transit.name: Mariposa Grove shuttle
transit.note: Free, every 15 minutes, 8 am – 7 pm; last bus leaves the grove at 8 pm. No ticket needed.

transit.name: Tuolumne Meadows shuttle
transit.note: Free, between the Meadows and Olmsted Point, 8 am – 4 pm.

transit.name: Hiker buses
transit.note: Tuolumne hikers bus once daily through Sep 13; the Glacier Point tour bus twice daily, a four-hour trip. Both paid, both bookable at TravelYosemite.com or the Lodge front desk. Glacier Point drops hikers one-way; no pickup at the point.

transit.name: YARTS
transit.note: Public transit into the park, with the seasonal routes ending on different dates: the Fresno (Highway 41) buses run through Sep 25; Sonora (Highway 120) and Mammoth Lakes (395) through Sep 30, though some of their runs ended Aug 31; Merced (Highway 140) year-round with multiple departures. Check the date for your route at YARTS.com or 877/989-2787.

transit.name: Bikes
transit.note: Over 11 miles of paved path on the Valley floor, 15 mph limit, helmets required under 18, and no bikes on hiking trails. Rentals 8 am – 7 pm at the Lodge, Curry Village, and Yosemite Village, 9 am – 6 pm from Sep 8; free bike share for one- to two-hour rides from the Village and Camp 4 lots, goyose.org/bikeshare.

transit.name: EV charging
transit.note: Level 2 only: Curry Village (20), Wawona Store (24), Yosemite Falls parking (10), the Lodge (8), The Ahwahnee (6), Welcome Center (4), El Portal (2). Tuolumne chargers are down.

essentials.title: Bears
essentials.text: Food storage is federal law: within arm's reach by day, out of the car and into a locker by night, and never in a truck bed or strapped to the outside. To a bear, food means anything with a scent, trash and toiletries included. Twenty-seven bears were hit by vehicles here last year, so hold the speed limit at dawn and dusk. Sightings: 209/372-0322.

essentials.title: Lightning
essentials.text: Afternoon thunderstorms run into September. Off the domes and exposed rim when storms build; shelter in a building or vehicle.

essentials.title: Smoke & fire
essentials.text: Fire season runs from here into October, and this is usually its worst stretch. Check air quality at fire.airnow.gov the morning you drive in, not the night before. Fires only in portable stoves, grills, and established rings, never unattended, and out cold before you walk away.

essentials.title: Wildlife
essentials.text: 150 feet from bears and coyotes, 25 feet from everything else. Feeding or approaching any animal is illegal, birds and squirrels included.

essentials.title: Heat & water
essentials.text: The Valley floor is still hot by late morning through early September, and Hetch Hetchy is worse. Walk early, carry a quart per person per two hours, and move uphill by noon. Nights in Tuolumne are cold year-round: pack a real layer.

essentials.title: Parking
essentials.text: Designated spaces or paved turnouts only, pulled fully off the road. Vehicles on vegetation get cited and towed.

essentials.title: Pets
essentials.text: Not allowed on trails, on shuttles, or inside buildings. Leashed on paved roads, paved bike paths, and the Mirror Lake road. Service dogs go anywhere visitors go; emotional support and therapy animals follow the pet rules.

essentials.title: The rules with teeth
essentials.text: Prohibited: drones, feeding or approaching wildlife, collecting plants, animals, or arrowheads, hunting, metal detectors, driving into meadows, biking off pavement, camping outside a designated campground, weapons inside federal buildings, and marijuana of any kind.

essentials.title: Camping
essentials.text: Every campground needs a reservation: Recreation.gov or 877/444-6777. Sleeping in a vehicle is legal only at a site you have booked, never at a roadside or in a parking lot.

essentials.title: Navigation
essentials.text: GPS gives wrong directions inside the park and routes people onto closed roads. Follow the road signs. There is no usable signal for most of Tioga Road or Glacier Point Road.

essentials.title: Wifi
essentials.text: Free at Degnan's Kitchen and the Mariposa County Library in the Valley, the El Portal Market, and the Wawona library. Hotel guests get it at the Lodge, Curry Village, and The Ahwahnee.
